title: Expansion Credit Velocity & Tiered Reset Policy — proposal and rollout plan
creator: Maya Singh
description:
Background: Large enterprise customers buying expansion commitments have varied consumption patterns after initial renewal — some ramp steadily, others spike then plateau. Current true-up and multi-year uplift rules assume either linear growth or static floors; that leads to frequent commercial exceptions and a poor operator experience for both sales and finance. Goal: introduce an 'expansion credit velocity' model with a tiered reset policy that standardizes how unused committed credits, overages, and mid-term expansions reconcile at renewal or within multi-year contracts. This proposal covers product definitions, pricing math, contract language, and an implementation rollout.

Proposal summary:
1) Expansion Credit Velocity (ECV): treat committed expansion credits as a time-phased pool. Each quarterly tranche has a velocity factor (Q1=1.0, Q2=0.9, Q3=0.8, Q4=0.7) that decays leftover credit value for purposes of renewal true-up calculation. Velocity factors reflect our observations that credits booked later in a commit period have lower predictability.
2) Tiered Reset Policy: introduce three reset options for enterprise contracts selectable at negotiation: Full Reset (unused credits expire), Partial Reset (carry forward up to 25% into next year at 50% value), Rolling Credit (unused credits convert to a one-time expansion credit usable within 12 months at 75% value). Pricing uplift for Partial Reset = +7% list uplift on committed amount, for Rolling Credit = +12% uplift.
3) True-up mechanics: at renewal or mid-term audit, reconcile actual consumption against net committed units after velocity adjustments and reset elections. Excess usage billed at overage rates; deficiency handled per contract (credit forfeiture or credited at adjusted value).

Options considered and trade-offs:
- Conservative approach (no carry): simplest to operate, lowest legal/commercial friction, highest churn risk.
- Aggressive carry policy (full carry at full value): very sales-friendly, increases revenue deferral and forecasting complexity.
- ECV + tiered reset (recommended): balances predictability and sales flexibility; reduces manual SAs and ad-hoc concessions.

Metrics / success criteria (measurable):
- Reduction in manual renewal concessions (%) target: 40% within two quarters.
- Forecast variance narrowness (net ARR vs expected): improve MAPE by 6 pts after first year.
- Number of commercial exceptions created by Finance/Legal: reduce by 50% vs baseline.

Implementation notes:
- Contract language: draft templates for each reset option (Legal & Sales to review) — initial drafts in Drive: https://drive.redwood/wip/pm/ecv-contract-drafts (private).
- Billing system changes: require flags to store reset election and quarterly velocity factors; small transform in invoice recon process (Billing PR: github.com/redwood/billing/pull/1423).
- Console/Invoice UX: add line-item visibility for velocity adjustments and reset elections; plan wireframes in Figma: https://redwood.design/file/ecv-wires.
- Pricing pages and sales playbook: update enablement materials, playbook with negotiation guidance and reference economic examples.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 0 (Pilot) — Q2 2026: offer to 10 strategic accounts (Sales-led); Finance and RevOps monitor reconciliation.
- Phase 1 (Controlled) — Q3 2026: enable as an optional clause for enterprise deals >$250k ARR.
- Phase 2 (GA) — Q4 2026: default catalog options with self-serve toggles for Dedicated/Private customers.

Risks & mitigations:
- Sales pushback on perceived complexity: mitigate with calculators and one-pagers; integrate into quoting flows with defaults.
- Legal/regulatory concerns for certain jurisdictions: Legal to run a compliance sweep per region prior to GA.
- Billing integration edge cases for mid-term upgrades: RevOps to own reconciliation runbooks and automated test coverage.

Required approvals: Product PM, Head of Sales Ops, Head of Finance, Legal. Draft approval thread started in Slack #renewals (link: slack.com/archives/C0456K/ecv-approval).
